A Swiss employment reference (Arbeitszeugnis) follows established formulas. The concordancer lets you check the exact meaning of a phrase before you reuse it.
The prohibition of competition has a precise legal definition. Its translation cannot be left to everyday usage.
Collective employment contracts exist in several official languages. Their terms can be checked in context in the Employment & Social Ins. domain.
An HR file contains personal data. Highly sensitive content mode requires storage and processing in Switzerland only.
Documents relating to work permits fall under another act, the Foreign Nationals and Integration Act, with its own vocabulary.

termes_note: The three ways of ending a contract have distinct names in the three official versions of the Code of Obligations. Confusing them in a translated letter can make the termination invalid. The English column uses the translation published by the Confederation on Fedlex where there is one, which has no legal force, and common usage otherwise.
lois_titre: The acts an employment contract cites every day
lois_intro: Swiss employment law is split between a contractual part, in the Code of Obligations, and a regulatory part, in the Employment Act. Personnel data and permits fall under yet other acts.

lois.note: Its Articles 319 to 362 govern the individual employment contract, termination, the reference and the collective employment contract; OR in German, CO in French and Italian.
It sets working hours, rest periods and health protection. Fedlex has no English translation: the English version of the CO uses this title. ArG in German, LTr in French.

lois.nom: Federal Act on Foreign Nationals and Integration
lois.note: It sets the conditions for employing foreign staff and for residence and work permits; AIG in German, LEI in French, LStrI in Italian.
It governs the employer's processing of personnel data; DSG in German, LPD in French and Italian.

who.p: A reference follows established formulas whose meaning recruiters know well. The concordancer shows these phrases in context, so that a literal translation does not change the message.

faq_titre: Frequently asked questions on employment law translation

faq.q: Does an employment contract have to be in the employee's language?
faq.r: The law does not require a particular language for the individual employment contract. But an employer who wants the commitment understood and enforceable has every interest in providing a version in the employee's working language. The platform's four languages (German, French, Italian and English) cover this need.

faq.q: How do I translate a termination letter safely?
faq.r: Distinguish the three regimes of the Code of Obligations: ordinary termination, wrongful termination and termination with immediate effect for good cause. The official terms exist in all three languages, and the letter itself justifies a Full review by a legal translator before it is sent.

faq.q: Can personnel files go through the platform?
faq.r: Yes, with the right mode. Storage is in Switzerland in every case, and Highly sensitive content mode requires processing in Switzerland only, with no reuse of the content in a memory. Engines hosted abroad display a warning before anything is sent.

faq.q: How do I keep staff regulations identical at every site?
faq.r: With the translation memory, which limits the work to the passages changed in a revision. And with terminology resources that belong to your organisation, which Fast lookup CHnell shows on top of its 30 sourced domains. Each term opens in context with its source before you fix it.

faq.q: Are collective employment contracts covered?
faq.r: Their vocabulary falls within the Employment & Social Ins. domain of the concordancer, with official sources. Each term opens in context with its reference, so you can check a concept before using it in a contract or in staff regulations.

faq.q: Can I quickly translate a simple internal memo?
faq.r: Yes. Text translation, in Text and document translation, accepts up to 10,000 pasted characters, with a choice of engine and up to four alternative wordings. For internal communication, a Light review is usually enough. For a document handed to an employee that might be produced later, a Full review is the safer choice.

description: Summary penalty orders, indictments, investigation files, mutual assistance: translate Swiss criminal proceedings in the terms of the SCC and CrimPC.
h1: Criminal proceedings, from one language to another
lead: Criminal proceedings are conducted in the language of the canton, but accused persons, witnesses and exhibits do not always speak it. Case files and summary penalty orders circulate in translation, and Corrext processes them in Switzerland.

promesses.d: summary penalty order, indictment, remand
up to 25 files of 50 MB per upload, original format preserved
Highly sensitive content mode: storage and processing in Switzerland

definition: Translating in Swiss criminal law means carrying over procedural documents whose legal nature is precise: summary penalty order, indictment, ruling abandoning proceedings, decision on detention. The Swiss Criminal Code (SCC) and the Criminal Procedure Code (CrimPC) are published in German, French and Italian. Each document has an official name in each of these languages.

facts.v: The file goes into File translation in batches and comes back in its original format, with pagination and exhibit numbering preserved.
A hearing conducted in one language is read in another by the defence. Translation helps you prepare; human review is for what you file.
The time limit for filing a rejection (Einsprache) is short. Instant translation of the pasted text lets you decide without waiting.
facts.s: Up to 10,000 characters per text translation.

facts.v: The indictment defines the subject matter of the trial. Its translation goes through a Full review, or Double review & certified translation if an attestation is required.
A request for mutual assistance is addressed to a foreign authority and must use its vocabulary as much as the Swiss vocabulary.
White-collar crime files mix statements, contracts and reports. The .xls and .xlsx formats are handled like Word documents.
Highly sensitive content mode requires storage and processing in Switzerland only, with no reuse of the content in a memory.
The Criminal Law and Litigation & Enforcement domains of the CHnell concordancer give the official usage of each term, with its source.

termes_titre: Criminal law vocabulary in four languages
termes_note: Italian does not model the names of procedural documents on French: the summary penalty order is a decreto d'accusa and the indictment an atto d'accusa. These equivalents are those of the official text. The English column uses the translation published by the Confederation on Fedlex where there is one, which has no legal force, and common usage otherwise.
lois_titre: The acts criminal proceedings cite every day
lois_intro: Swiss criminal law rests on a substantive code and a procedural code unified since 2011. International mutual assistance and the fight against money laundering add their own acts and their own vocabulary.

lois.note: It defines offences and penalties, from offences against property to money laundering; StGB in German, CP in French and Italian.
It governs the investigation, procedural acts, detention and trial in every canton; StPO in German, CPP in French and Italian.

lois.nom: Federal Act on International Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters
lois.note: It governs requests made to Switzerland, or by Switzerland to a foreign state; IRSG in German, EIMP in French.

lois.nom: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
lois.note: It sets the obligations whose breach gives rise to many white-collar crime proceedings; GwG in German, LBA in French, LRD in Italian.

who.p: The case is investigated in German and the accused is defended by a lawyer from French-speaking Switzerland. Batches go into File translation in Highly sensitive content mode, and the defence reads everything before choosing which documents to have reviewed.

who.p: The request must be understood by a foreign authority while staying true to the legal classifications of Swiss law. The concordancer shows the terms of the SCC and the CrimPC in context, and the version sent goes through a Full review.

faq_titre: Frequently asked questions on criminal law translation

faq.q: Can a machine translation be filed in the case record?
faq.r: It serves first to understand. A document filed with the criminal justice authority must be reliable and, depending on the case, attested. It then goes through a Full review by a legal translator, or Double review & certified translation when the court requires a certified translation.

faq.q: How do I protect the confidentiality of the investigation?
faq.r: Storage is on Swiss servers in every case. Highly sensitive content mode also requires processing in Switzerland only, with no reuse of the content in a translation memory. Engines hosted abroad display a warning before anything is sent.

faq.q: Are the names of procedural documents harmonised?
faq.r: The Criminal Procedure Code has applied throughout Switzerland since 2011 and is published in the three official languages, which fixes the name of each document. The concordancer shows these occurrences in context, with their source, in the Criminal Law and Litigation & Enforcement domains.

faq.q: Can I process a case file of several thousand pages?
faq.r: Yes, in batches: up to 25 files of 50 MB per upload in Text and document translation, or through a translation project for end-to-end tracking with quote and review. Documents come back in their original format, which preserves exhibit numbering.

faq.q: What about scanned or poor-quality documents?
faq.r: The PDF to Word tab converts a scanned PDF into an editable Word document before translation or annotation. This is common for seized documents, old correspondence and annexes sent as images by a foreign authority. The resulting document is then translated like a native file.

faq.q: Which languages for international proceedings?
faq.r: German, French, Italian and English are native in every pair, and the platform covers 30 languages in total. The legal classifications, however, remain those of Swiss law, which the concordancer lets you check article by article. Documents come back in their original format, whatever the source language.
